candidates.title: The Booth-Side Treaty
candidates.suggested_text_hook: no discussion. she gets the booth side.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It gives one partner a soft little instruction and the other partner a proud 'I already know' moment. The send-trigger is immediate for couples with restaurant seating rituals.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Comments will split into warm claims like 'as she should,' 'he learned,' and 'booth side is the princess seat.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: A fast 'babe this is us' send, especially from people who have one tiny non-negotiable on dates.

candidates.title: Leaving In Five
candidates.suggested_text_hook: leaving in five means seven tiny things first.
candidates.why_people_may_share: The tag reason is clean: one partner is always at the door, the other is still doing micro-tasks that suddenly feel urgent.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: It baits affectionate confession: 'guilty,' 'the plant needed water,' 'checking the stove counts,' and 'he just stands there with keys.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Couples will recognize the exact doorway tension without it becoming a fight; it is teasing, not cruel.

candidates.title: The Photo Approval Committee
candidates.suggested_text_hook: he took 47 photos. she approved two.
candidates.why_people_may_share: It lets people lovingly call out the partner who becomes patient tripod, lighting assistant, and morale support in public.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm comment bait is obvious: 'only two is generous,' 'he knows my angles now,' 'training complete,' and 'justice for the photographer.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Highly taggable, especially for couples where one person has quietly become the official date photographer.

candidates.title: The Tiny Bowl Incident
candidates.suggested_text_hook: we came for one thing. she found a tiny bowl.
candidates.why_people_may_share: The send-trigger is the partner who turns a quick errand into a small emotional adoption of an unnecessary object.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will name their version: tiny bowl, candle, mug, plant, notebook. It invites specific confessions instead of generic 'cute.'
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: A soft guilty laugh from anyone whose partner has watched them fall in love with a random little object in a shop.

engagement_rationale: Top pick because it is instantly readable, visually stageable, and gives both sides a reason to send: one as recognition, one as a gentle reminder. It has stronger brand warmth than a pure complaint post, and the comment lane is already alive: 'as she should,' 'he knows,' 'that side is mine.'
distribution_risks: The Photo Approval Committee can drift into overused boyfriend-photographer meme territory unless the scene stays intimate and specific.
Leaving In Five must stay affectionate; avoid framing one partner as incompetent or annoying.
The Tiny Bowl Incident needs tactile visual charm so it does not become a generic shopping joke.
The Booth-Side Treaty should show care through body language, not turn into princess entitlement or caption-only romance.
